233 and 307 mV overpotentials are required for the pure NiFe LDH

we further evaluated the HER activity of the hybrid electrode in 1 M KOH... (iR-corrected)... overpotentials of 116 and 192 mV to achieve current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm^{-2}... nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows 3D macroporous structure of Cu@NiFe LDH with uniform core-shell nanostructure where NiFe LDH nanosheets vertically grow on Cu NWs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2a is the SEM image of the Cu@NiFe LDH in low magnification, which shows the 3D macroporous structure covered by uniform nanomaterials on the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals core-shell nanostructure with ~700 nm diameter hybrid, ~200 nm Cu NW core, ~250 nm NiFe LDH shell, and NiFe LDH nanosheets of 3.2-4 nm thickness (4-5 layers).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diameter of the core-shell hybrid is ∼700 nm with ∼200 nm core of Cu NWs and ∼250 nm shell of NiFe LDH NSs.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringe with interplanar spacing of 0.25 nm assigned to (012) plane of NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Distinctive lattice fringe with an interplanar spacing of 0.25 nm (inset in Fig. 2f) was also identified, which can be assigned to the (012) plane of NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS line scan and mapping confirm core-shell structure with Cu in central part and Ni, Fe homogeneously distributed throughout Cu@NiFe LDH composites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) line scanning results (Fig. 2g) and EDS mapping analysis (Fig. 2h) further identify the quintessential core-shell structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of Cu NWs shows cubic Cu peaks at 43.34°, 50.48°, 74.17° (PDF#65-9026) with no CuO or Cu2O peaks; Cu@NiFe LDH shows additional small LDH peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3a, three strong peaks located at 43.34°, 50.48°, and 74.17° all corresponds to the cubic-structured Cu (PDF#65-9026).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Cu, Ni, Fe, O, C elements; Ni 2p peaks at 855.6 eV (2p3/2) and 873.3 eV (2p1/2); Fe 2p peaks at 712.7 eV (2p3/2) and 725.9 eV (2p1/2) indicate Ni2+ and Fe3+ states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 3c, the two peaks located at binding energies of 855.6 and 873.3 eV correspond to Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2, respectively... two prominent peaks located at 712.7 and 725.9 eV are assigned to Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV measurements determine double-layer capacitance Cdl = 59.8 mF cm⁻² for Cu@NiFe LDH (vs 13.5 mF cm⁻² for pure NiFe LDH), indicating significantly larger electrochemically active surface area (ECSA).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cu@NiFe LDH electrode possesses the highest Cdl of 59.8 mF cm⁻², which is nearly 4.5 and 5.5 times that of the pure NiFe LDH (13.5 mF cm⁻²) and Cu NWs (11.2 mF cm⁻²), respectively, demonstrating the improved ECSA...

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS at 250 mV overpotential shows charge transfer resistance Rct ≈ 2.8 Ω for Cu@NiFe LDH (vs 12 Ω for NiFe LDH, 15 Ω for Cu NWs), indicating superior charge transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 4f, the Cu@NiFe LDH electrode possess a much smaller charge transfer resistance (Rct) of ∼2.8Ω, in contrast to the pure NiFe LDH (12 Ω) and Cu NWs (15 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER stability test TEM confirms core-shell nanostructure of Cu@NiFe LDH is well preserved with (012) NiFe LDH lattice spacing of 0.25 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image in Fig. 6a reveals that the core-shell nanostructure of Cu NWs and NiFe LDH NSs is well preserved. Moreover, the interplanar spacing of 0.25 nm corresponding to the (012) plane of NiFe LDH is still observed (Fig. 6b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER stability test EDS mapping confirms intact core-shell structure of Cu@NiFe LDH with homogeneous elemental distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping images in Fig. 6c further confirm the intact core-shell structure with homogeneous distribution of the elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER/HER stability test XPS shows Ni 2p and Fe 2p spectra nearly identical to fresh sample (Ni²⁺, Fe³⁺ states preserved); Cu 2p shows stronger peaks with CuO satellites indicating minor Cu oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figs 6d and 6e, the high-resolution XPS spectra of Ni 2p and Fe 2p... are almost identical to that of the fresh sample... the peaks for the high-resolution XPS spectrum of Cu 2p (Fig. S17c) become stronger after OER stability test, and the two satellite peaks confirm the existence of CuO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability test XRD pattern of Cu@NiFe LDH matches initial pattern with no phase change of NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD pattern of the Cu@NiFe LDH catalysts after stability test (Fig. S17a) also matches well with the initial one, indicating no phase change of NiFe LDH after OER and HER tests.
